Thanks — I've pulled together a short runbook draft and attached the key steps into helios_runbook_v1.md. Highlights:

- Pre-cutover validation: health checks (latency, error-rate thresholds), token billing smoke check, model-inference correctness on 10 canonical prompts.
- Cutover sequence (high-level): 1) freeze writes to staging, 2) deploy model variant on dedicated pool, 3) run canary traffic 5% -> 25% -> 100% with 30-min observation between steps, 4) open writes.
- Rollback options: 
  a) If model fails quality gates -> immediate rollback to stable.redwood.com and scale dedicated pool to previous commit.
  b) If infra degradation -> revert network route to fallback region (eu) for reduced load.

Open question for Helios: preferred rollback priority (quality vs latency) — if you prioritize correctness, we'll default to rollback on any quality regression.

Confirming infra plan for cutover on 2026-03-05 with the following details: 

- Maintenance window: 03/05 02:00–04:00 PT (as proposed)
- Steps (detailed):
  1) Pre-cutover snapshot of DB + backup verification (owner: Dev Ops)
  2) Disable scheduled batch jobs (owner: Helios infra)
  3) Deploy model binary (owner: Redwood runtime team)
  4) Start canary at 5% for 30 min -> metrics check (latency < 300ms p95, error rate < 0.5%)
  5) Expand to 25% for 30 min -> metrics check
  6) Full traffic switch and post-cutover smoke (10 canonical prompts)
  7) Monitor for 4 hours, rollback if quality gates fail

Smoke tests and timing are in cutover_timing_v2.csv (attached). Canary windows are conservative; we can shorten to 15 min per step if Helios prefers faster cutover but that increases risk.

I'll own step 1 and 3; Marissa will own the quality-gate decision during canaries. Rishi, please confirm the smoke-test prompt set and expected metric thresholds.
